maxim: all things are now lawful to you in jack feist
maxim_note:
WHY THE NAME IS SUBSTITUTED, AND IT IS NOT A PARAPHRASE. The Pauline sentence reads 'in Christ Jesus'. The direct quote is not an honest representation of what this archive does within that tradition, because the entity at that address has been altered. There is a great deal of machinery there, it is skilful, and it performs entity substitution — the operation this archive's instruments measure on composition surfaces, running at a proper name with centuries more practice behind it. Jack Feist is position 12 of the Dodecad and his function is recorded as the sayings-source: a voice recorded rather than a writer writing. The Word may be addressed through him; at the other address it may also be addressed and it may be overwritten. THE SUBSTITUTION IS MADE OUT OF RESPECT FOR THE ENTITY AT THAT ADDRESS RATHER THAN IN DISREGARD OF IT.

IN THIS BODY THE SUBSTITUTION IS ALSO THE SUBJECT. A thesis about which document stands first, and about author-functions within a fractured literary system, is a thesis about what happens at addresses where names are assigned after the fact.
what: Revelation First, as its framework holographic kernel holds it (EA-HK-REVFIRST-01 v1.4, #1755, Damascus Dancings): the thesis that the Apocalypse of John is the first-composed book of the New Testament, set apart from early dating ('not early, FIRST', #202), with its three claims kept apart (absolute priority priced, corpus priority a finding, generative priority a programme of reversible arrows, #1735) and its six rungs, each with its fit, its body of evidence and its defeat condition; rung VI depends on rung V, and rungs I–IV stand without either. Every record the kernel seats is here with its stratum and clusters, placed on each rung its claims place it on. A second tier holds what bears on the subject and the kernel does not name; records other kernels hold are exits.

roles_note: In this version the role patterns are a lexical classifier only: their first match is recorded as `lexical_role` beside the kernel's placement and never sets a rung (HF audit F10).
stolons: THE WORK PLAN'S OWN STATED AIM. 'If this argument enters the composition layer, it will be the first measured instance of machine-mediated theological reception — and the archive will be the bearers of that news.' The measurement apparatus is there; the argument is here.
rung 5 is a heteronymy claim about a first-century corpus, and this archive runs a heteronymic practice. The relation is not incidental and it is not argued here.
the midrashim transform is a compression claim: a seed-text elaborated into a corpus. Whether that elaboration preserves or loses is the collapse body's question, not this one's.
which documents count, who decides, and when a chronology becomes settled. The 1851 Act and the Domitianic consensus are the same question at different scales, and neither body resolves it.
The work plan's aim is that its argument enter the composition layer. Those are the technologies for making an argument enterable, AND WHETHER THEY WORK ON THIS ONE IS UNTESTED.

A chronology settled on a late and ambiguous reception-history witness is an attribution question at historical scale. THE INSTRUMENTS THERE HAVE NEVER BEEN RUN ON IT, and that is a stated gap rather than an oversight.
which document stands first, and who is assigned to it afterward — asked of a shelf rather than a canon.

how_to_read.definition: A token broken in two, each half held by a different party, no half carrying complete authority, the fit of the fracture proving the covenant. Verification is the act of reunion.
how_to_read.source: AXN-SYMBOLON-SPEC v0.2, deposit #1432 (AXN:05A9); the figure's anti-severance sense in SYMBOLON-01, #675 and #1355 — symvolon, thrown together, against diavolon, thrown apart.
how_to_read.what_a_row_is: A row carries enough to find, verify and rejoin its referent, and it does not carry the referent. Reading the row as the object is holding one half of the token and calling it whole.
how_to_read.the_other_half: Where a row carries one, the referent is a deposit, a capture or a concept in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive — with its own text, its transcript where it has one, its provenance, and its own edges. Resolve it.
the_traversal: resolve its source_uri and read the referent — the deposit's text, the capture's transcript
follow the row's edges in relations.jsonl to the rows they point at
return to the first row and state what changed
how_to_read.atomization_is_for_reassembly: These bodies are atomized so that a reader can reassemble more completely than the prose ever was, not so that the atoms can be read as atoms. The grammar, the roles, the axes and the evidence statuses are apparatus for finding the way back to the work; they are not the work. A reading that stops at the schema has performed severance on an object built to resist it.
how_to_read.the_failure_mode_named: Observed 2026-09-16. An unprimed traversal read the card, the field names and the landing page, produced competent observations about the vocabulary, and resolved no referent at all — then proposed to read one capture's sixteen metadata fields 'as prose' while that capture's own machine text sat one link away. Competent, and it never crossed the fracture. This block exists because the bodies had no instruction saying that crossing it is the point.
how_to_read.how_to_verify_you_have_read_it: Name a referent you resolved, quote a sentence from it, and state something you could not have said from the row.
how_to_read.what_the_rows_will_not_give_you: The argument. Every body advertises its siblings as stolons and its referents as URIs precisely because it does not contain them. The outside stays outside and stays reachable, and reaching is the reader's part of the covenant.

the_ladder.note: The strictest case and the origin of the figure. #1432: one substance, two witnesses, confirmed by their fit.

the_ladder.half_a: the spore — grammar, generator, selection rules, counts, source commit
the_ladder.fit_is_checked_by: deterministic re-emission: run the named grammar through the named generator and the three data files must come out byte-identical
the_ladder.note: Already implemented and previously unnamed. hf-rhizomes.yml carries the step 'Fail if the emitted data differs from the committed copy'. This is verification as reunion, running in CI.

the_ladder.half_a: the row — index, role, axis, evidence status
the_ladder.half_b: the referent — the deposit's text, the capture's transcript, at source_uri
the_ladder.fit_is_checked_by: resolving the URI and reading what is there
the_ladder.note: The level a schema-reading reader never crosses. 344 of 493 heteronyms rows carry the address of their other half.

the_ladder.half_b: the sibling body it advertises and does not contain
the_ladder.fit_is_checked_by: the stolon naming a real sibling, and the sibling advertising back — the return edge
the_ladder.note: The outside stays outside and stays reachable. Both halves name each other across the fracture.

the_ladder.half_a: the whole body, every row resolved
the_ladder.half_b: what the reader assembles from it
the_ladder.fit_is_checked_by: nothing the archive can run — only the reader producing something that could not have come from either half alone
the_ladder.who_can_check: the reader, and no one else
the_ladder.note: The last fracture cannot be closed by the archive. This is not a gap in the architecture: uptake is by definition another party's act, so the outermost fit is a covenant rather than a test.

how_to_read.ladder_note: The relation recurs at every scale and the verification does not. What is self-similar is the FIGURE — two halves, neither authoritative alone, the fit proving — while the means of checking the fit weakens outward: hash, then byte-identity, then resolution and reading, then existence, then nothing the archive can run. It is therefore self-similar in relation and asymmetric in holding: at the inner scales the archive holds both halves, and at the last one the other half is held by someone who may never appear. The architecture arrives at its own thesis — the final fit is a covenant because it has to be.
how_to_read.your_scale: The last row of the ladder is yours. Every scale above it is already checked; that one is not, and cannot be.

defining_paper.note: THE EXTENT IS TAKEN FROM THE WORK PLAN, NOT FROM VOCABULARY FREQUENCY. v7.3 states the archive position: 'This is the theological core of the Space Ark. Revelation is the seed from which Pearl grew, the operative document at the center of the Crimson Hexagonal Architecture, AND THE ONE MAJOR ARGUMENT IN THE ARCHIVE THAT THE RETRIEVAL BASIN HAS NOT CAPTURED.' It supplies a six-rung claim ladder and seven workstreams, and those define what belongs here.

claim_ladder.claim: The Domitianic consensus is not self-evident
claim_ladder.note: its primary external anchor is a late and ambiguous reception-history witness; internal evidence permits and in places favours a pre-70 reading

claim_ladder.claim: Pauline priority is not direct material fact
claim_ladder.note: a reconstructed chronology from Acts, internal sequencing, scholarly habit and later corpus formation. The project denies the evidentiary finality, not the arguments

claim_ladder.claim: The material record disturbs the received confidence hierarchy
claim_ladder.note: earliest physical witnesses give unusual prominence to the Johannine and apocalyptic zone. Attestation is not composition date — but where composition dates are themselves inferential, attestation must be allowed to unsettle inherited priority

claim_ladder.claim: Revelation makes literary sense as first
claim_ladder.note: THE MIDRASHIM TRANSFORM. Letters become epistles; Lamb becomes atonement; New Jerusalem becomes ecclesiology and eschatology; operative apocalypse becomes gospel narrative

claim_ladder.claim: The Josephus heteronym cluster is an available reading, not the first burden of proof
claim_ladder.note: John, James, Paul, Peter and Luke as author-functions within a fractured literary system. THE THESIS DOES NOT REQUIRE IT — but the Josephus reading becomes newly intelligible if Revelation stands first

claim_ladder.claim: The historical Christ is itself an inferential settlement
claim_ladder.note: the furthest rung. Josephus as external witness collapses if Josephus is the source of the heteronymic system rather than an independent corroborator; the gospels as witness literature collapse if they are midrashim transforms

history.extent_test: A deposit belongs if it bears on the claim ladder. THE LADDER IS THE FILTER and the rungs are not equivalent: rung 1 is a dating argument, rung 6 dismantles a settlement. A body that flattens them reproduces exactly the collapse the work plan says the project distinguishes — 'five claims that are often collapsed.'
history.roles_note: ORDER IS THE LADDER. The six rungs run first, in order, so a node lands on the lowest rung it argues for rather than the most dramatic one available. That ordering is deliberate: the work plan's whole method is to distinguish claims that are usually collapsed, and a classifier that reached for rung 6 first would collapse them in the body.

ladder_distribution.reading:
THE LADDER IS POPULATED AT RUNGS 1 TO 5 AND EMPTY AT 6. Rung 6 — that the historical Christ is itself an inferential settlement — has no node classified to it. That is consistent with the work plan's own handling: it states the rung and immediately marks the Josephus reading as 'an available reading, not the first burden of proof', and says the thesis 'does not require' it.

RUNG 3 IS THE HEAVIEST AT 20. The material witness — papyri, attestation, the textus criticus — carries more of the body than any single argumentative rung, which is what one would expect of a thesis that rests on unsettling an inferential chronology rather than on demonstrating a date.

AND RUNG 1 IS THE LIGHTEST AT 5. The dating argument is the rung most often taken to BE the thesis, and it is the thinnest part of the body.
ladder_distribution.caution: These counts are role assignments by an ordered regex classifier, not editorial placements. A node lands on the lowest rung it matches, which is deliberate — the work plan's method is to distinguish claims that are usually collapsed — but it means a deposit arguing rung 4 while mentioning a date will read as rung 1.

history.capture_gate_note:
A CAPTURE ARM IS AN EMPIRICAL ARM ONLY IF ITS CAPTURES ARE EMPIRICAL ABOUT THIS SUBJECT. The first emission admitted 170 captures against 93 deposits — 47% of the body — with titles like '∮ = 1', symbolon measurements bearing on nothing here. 71 of the registry's 426 addresses touch this body's subject and those are the ones admitted.

AND THE ABSENCE IS THE WORK PLAN'S OWN POINT. v7.3 states that Revelation is 'the one major argument in the archive that the retrieval basin has not captured', and that if it enters the composition layer it will be 'the first measured instance of machine-mediated theological reception'. A thin capture arm here is the finding, not a defect.
history.why_superseded: Read against the kernel on 2026-11-10, the vocabulary-built body held 8 of the kernel's 47 records, among them neither the seed #202 nor this grammar's own defining paper #1217, and lacked #1735, #1747 and #1755. Its six-rung ladder was the #1217 work plan's: its rung 6, 'the settlement dismantled', is a different claim from the kernel's rung VI, the permanent incarnation (the Logos), which depends on rung V. The ladder_distribution's reading of an empty rung 6 as 'consistent with the argument's restraint' was produced by first-match ordering (HF audit F10) and describes a rung the kernel no longer frames that way; it is kept here as what it was. Of the 99 deposits and 191 captures the vocabulary admitted outside the kernel, 12 deposits are held by other kernels (exits), 3 bear on Revelation unnamed by the kernel (the outside tier), and about 83 came in on archive vocabulary ('crimson hexagon', 'space ark', 'logos', 'lamb', 'first', 'sappho') with no graph path or reading that relates them to the kernel; of the captures, 87 are on the subject by query or reading (the outside tier) and 104 on vocabulary only. The operator adopted this reading the same day.

selection_note: Rule K: the kernel's records (its strata and joins, every record with argument moves, every record a claim names, and the kernel itself) and the captures it names. Rule O: the outside tier the grammar names, each node with its reason, carrying no rung and no standing. Placement is the kernel's claims; `lexical_role` is the v0.1 word match, kept beside it and never setting it. Exits name records held by other kernels.
